# Capacity analysis (generated by analysis/capacity.py)

Analytic estimate, not a simulation result. 802.11g ERP-OFDM timing is approximate and utilization ignores collisions and retries, so real saturation starts earlier than shown. Replace the exchange times with INET's measured values from a single-AMR, no-load run.

Assumed traffic: state 1000 B at 10 Hz per AMR (uplink); orders 600 B at 5 Hz per AMR (downlink, shares the same medium); 4 stations send 1400 B telemetry over the wire only.

## 1. Airtime per successful exchange

| PHY rate | ACK rate | State exchange, CSMA (us) | Order exchange, CSMA (us) | State exchange, scheduled cw=0 (us) | Max state packets/s (CSMA) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 54 Mbps | 24 Mbps | 326 | 266 | 258 | 3072 |
| 24 Mbps | 24 Mbps | 521 | 390 | 454 | 1918 |
| 12 Mbps | 12 Mbps | 882 | 618 | 814 | 1134 |
| 6 Mbps | 6 Mbps | 1606 | 1074 | 1538 | 623 |

CSMA exchange includes DIFS, the mean backoff (CWmin/2 slots), preamble, data, SIFS and ACK. The scheduled column has zero backoff. Its value is the minimum slot length for the largest wireless frame (state); add a safety margin when you choose `slotDuration`.

## 3. Fleet size that reaches a target utilization

| Target | 54 Mbps | 24 Mbps | 12 Mbps | 6 Mbps |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 10% | 22 | 14 | 8 | 5 |
| 30% | 65 | 42 | 25 | 14 |
| 60% | 131 | 84 | 50 | 28 |
| 90% | 196 | 126 | 76 | 42 |

Reading: with the placeholder rates, a 54 Mbps cell stays lightly loaded for the whole 5-40 AMR range, so 802.11 contention is unlikely to dominate. To observe it, lower the PHY rate, extend the fleet range, or raise per-AMR traffic (real VDA 5050 state sizes and rates are the open question, decisions.md Q6).

## 4. Wired offered load on the switch-to-FMS port (100 Mbps)

| N (AMRs) | State (Mbps) | + telemetry 2000 us (22.4 Mbps) | + telemetry 600 us (74.7 Mbps) | + telemetry 300 us (149.3 Mbps) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 5 | 0.4 | 23.9 | 78.8 | 157.2 |
| 10 | 0.9 | 24.4 | 79.3 | 157.7 |
| 20 | 1.7 | 25.2 | 80.1 | 158.5 |
| 40 | 3.4 | 26.9 | 81.8 | 160.2 |
| 80 | 6.8 | 30.4 | 85.2 | 163.6 |
| 120 | 10.3 | 33.8 | 88.7 | 167.1 |
| 200 | 17.1 | 40.6 | 95.5 | 173.9 |

Values include headers and the 12 B gap. Under TAS, telemetry fits 4 frames per 500 us window, a payload ceiling of about 44.8 Mbps, so TAS cells throttle telemetry by design while FIFO carries it up to link saturation.

Orders on the switch-to-AP port: N=5: 0.13 Mbps, N=10: 0.27 Mbps, N=20: 0.54 Mbps, N=40: 1.07 Mbps, N=80: 2.14 Mbps, N=120: 3.22 Mbps, N=200: 5.36 Mbps. With the placeholder GCL the orders window carries at most 1 frame per 1 ms cycle (1000 orders/s), so check it against N x 5 orders/s.
